coverage_questions: The paper does not provide separate input-processing specifications for all 32 atlas routes or 22 configurations.
The paper does not document a separate input path for PROCYON-SPLIT beyond the documented train/test split and evaluation use; its architecture is described through the shared PROCYON framework.
The internal tokenization and embedding procedures of ESM-2 3B, GearNet, and Llama-3-8B are unspecified.
The paper does not establish the algebra or ordering used to form unified multimodal tokens from text, sequence, and structure representations.
The paper does not document the internal encoding path for small-molecule structures or the exact candidate-domain decomposition used in drug-domain retrieval.

The paper names PROCYON-BIND as a PDBBind-fine-tuned configuration, while the atlas seed lists PROCYON and PROCYON-SPLIT; this assembly includes PROCYON-BIND because it is explicitly documented in the paper.
Exact prompt templates, special tokens, attention masks, causal-label construction, and sampling distributions are unspecified.
The paper does not specify how protein libraries, domain libraries, or peptide candidates are represented before scoring or ranking.

The paper does not document a distinct input path for every downstream application; application-specific trajectories reuse the documented PROCYON architecture only where the source explicitly supports that reuse.

The paper documents QA-score filtering for phenotype generation, but does not establish the QA scoring computation, filter algebra, threshold, or ordering. The assembly therefore preserves these as opaque scoring and documented selection boundaries.

evidence.quote: In protein retrieval, PROCYON retrieves a ranked list of proteins that match a user's prompt. First, the protein language model processes protein sequences and projects them into the unified latent space via a retrieval-specific projector. The natural language prompt is then processed by the LLM and projected into the unified latent space by a query connector, allowing PROCYON to identify the proteins most closely related to the projected prompt (Supplementary Note 1, Extended Data Figure 1).

PROCYON is a multimodal protein foundation model with 11 billion parameters. Composed of a Llama-3-8B language model [31] and encoders for protein sequence (ESM-2 3B [32]) and structure (GearNet [19]), PROCYON can process inputs of natural language and protein sequence and structure.

evidence.quote: In phenotype generation, PROCYON generates natural language descriptions of protein phenotypes conditioned on the user's prompt. The prompt is split into multimodal components: the text is tokenized via a standard text tokenizer, and the protein sequence and structure are encoded via the modality-specific encoders. These multimodal tokens form a unified prompt that is then processed by the LLM, enabling phenotype generation via standard language model sampling techniques. We also leverage PROCYON's text generation capability for question-answering (QA), where the model is asked whether the phenotype and protein are associated, prompting a 'yes' or 'no' response. These QA scores are also used as a filtering mechanism (Methods Sec. 2.3, Extended Data Figure 2) to improve phenotype generation (Extended Data Figure 3).

PROCYON is a multimodal protein foundation model with 11 billion parameters. Composed of a Llama-3-8B language model [31] and encoders for protein sequence (ESM-2 3B [32]) and structure (GearNet [19]), PROCYON can process inputs of natural language and protein sequence and structure.
